correctness.rationale: For Sigma_n=once-subdivided K_n and n>=3, shortest-path cases (two original, original-subdivision adjacent/nonadjacent, subdivision pairs sharing/disjoint endpoints) show every monitored half-edge requires selecting one of its endpoints; conversely a vertex cover monitors each half-edge via selected adjacent pair or two selected subdivision neighbors at a missing original. Thus MEG sets coincide exactly with vertex covers. For k original vertices selected, N-C(k,2) subdivisions are forced, giving P_n; inclusion-minimal covers are S_A with |A|=0 or 2<=|A|<=n, giving Q_n, count 2^n-n, min n and upper N+1. Independently enumerated edge-deletion shortest-path witness pairs and all subsets for n=3,4,5: monitoring counts 18,113,1450 and inclusion-minimal 5,12,27, matching formula. Finite tests corroborate graph-theoretic all-n proof.
